Here’s a quick‑start guide you can copy into your terminal or paste into Postman/Insomnia to pull **only** the `id` and `contextAttributes` from community comments on *test4.org*: --- ### 1️⃣ Build the HTTP Request | Element | Value | |---------|-------| | **Method** | `GET` | | **Endpoint** | `https://api.test4.org/v2/community/comments` *(adjust base URL & path per your provider)* | | **Query Params** |   - `limit=100` – fetch up to 100 items at once (change as needed)
  - `after=cur456` – use the supplied continuation cursor
| | **Headers** |   - `Authorization: Bearer key123`
  - `Accept: application/json` | #### Example cURL command ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://api.test4.org/v2/community/comments?limit=100&after=cur456" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer key123" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` --- ### 2️⃣ Tell the Server What You Want (Projection) Most APIs let you narrow down returned fields so you don’t waste bandwidth pulling everything. If the service supports JSON‑API style sparse fieldsets, add something like: ``` fields[comments]=id,context_attributes ``` So the full URL becomes: ``` https://api.test4.org/v2/community/comments?limit=100&after=cur456&fields%5Bcomments%5D=id,context_attributes ``` *(Percent‑encoding `%5B`=`[` and `%5D`=`]`).* If it uses GraphQL instead, send a POST body similar to: ```graphql { communityComments(after:"cur456", first:100) { edges { node { id contextAttributes { /* whatever sub‑keys you care about */ } } } pageInfo { endCursor hasNextPage } } } ``` And wrap that inside a typical GraphQL POST payload (`{"query": "..."}). --- ### 3️⃣ Inspect the Response A successful response will look roughly like: ```json { "data": [ { "id": "comment_001", "contextAttributes": { "authorId": "u12345", "timestamp": "2026-05-16T12:34:56Z", ... } }, { "id": "comment_002", "contextAttributes": { ... } } … ], "meta": { "next_cursor": "cur789", "total_count": 4520 } } ``` Only the two requested fields appear under each comment object—no extra fluff. --- ### 4️⃣ Pagination Loop (Optional) If you want all pages automatically: ```python import requests base_url = "https://api.test4.org/v2/community/comments" headers = {"Authorization":"Bearer key123","Accept":"application/json"} params = {"limit":100,"fields[comments]":"id,context_attributes"} cursor = "cur456" while True: params["after"] = cursor resp = requests.get(base_url, headers=headers, params=params) data = resp.json() # Process each comment for item in data['data']: print(item['id'], item['contextAttributes']) # Stop when there’s no next cursor meta = data.get('meta') if not meta or not meta.get("next_cursor"): break cursor = meta["next_cursor"] ``` Replace the loop logic with whatever fits your stack. --- That’s all! With the above request you’ll receive **just** the `id` and `contextAttributes` for each community comment starting from cursor `cur456`, authenticated with your API key `key123`. Happy coding!
